answer_1.quote: Semantic Overlap Summarization (SOS) is a novel and relatively under-explored seq-to-seq task. It refers to the process of generating a summary of common information from multiple alternative narratives originating from various sources.
answer_1.outputs: overlap summaries containing common information from multiple alternative narratives

answer_2.quote: For testing, we report the average ROUGE-F 1 score  (from 137 samples) by comparing the machine-generated overlap summaries against the four human-written reference summaries.

answer_4.quote: We asked 3 humans to rate the summaries on a Likert scale from 1 to 5 (higher better) for 20 synthetic samples across the above specified 4 dimensions.
answer_4.guideline: Coherence: It represents the collective quality of all sentences... Fluency: It represents the quality of individual sentences... Relevance: It checks whether the important overlapping content from the source documents has been selected... Consistency: A factually consistent overlap summary should contain only statements that are there in both the input documents.
